summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments from automated reviewers by triaging, fixing, and formally resolving each thread.
summary.outcome: All 4 unresolved review threads were addressed with fixes to pr-release-preview.js, post-merge-release.js, and release-please.yml, then committed and pushed.

repo: Comment matching in postOrUpdateComment was author-agnostic — it matched by HTML marker only, risking updates to comments not owned by the bot.
pr-release-preview.js label removal logic was too broad, clearing manually-added labels for non-computed components.
release-please.yml only cleared --latest=false for the root tag, not all manifest releases.
Stale 'pre-installed' comments existed in both pr-release-preview.js and post-merge-release.js.

code.finding: Label removal did not exclude manually-added labels for non-computed components.
Stale 'pre-installed' comment that no longer reflected current behavior.
Same stale 'pre-installed' comment mirrored from pr-release-preview.js.
--latest=false was only cleared for the root tag; manifest releases were not covered.

workflow: PR review threads can be resolved via GraphQL mutation resolveReviewThread; replies use REST with --field for integer params like in_reply_to.
Triage table (valid fix / already addressed / not applicable) is an effective pattern before implementing any changes.
All fixes should be batched before running tests, then committed together rather than incrementally.

open_items: E2E tests were not run — only typecheck was executed before committing; E2E coverage for these workflow/script changes is deferred.
Thread replies and formal GraphQL resolution are not shown in the transcript — unclear if all threads were actually marked resolved.
